main_text.p: dere, manducare, Sax. /Ætan; al.eᵹan, unde nostrum to eate, illo sensu: Teutonicis aet & aes. Edax Saxonibus /Ætulman [?].
Asca, Cinis] Saxonibus /Æxe; pluraliter /Æxan, aɥran [?]. Hoc Belgis modernis Asche; nobis hodie Ashes. Unde de Cineralia, Ashwednesday dicimus; Belg. Aschenwoensdach.
Andzan, vel Andarn, In vanum: nonne Italorum est Indarno?
Asgetalt, Oblivioni] Vocabulum (ut videtur) ejusdem prosapiæ ac Sax. ofenzÿtolnerre, quod eádem venit acceptione; nobis hodie, forgetful-nesse. Belg. vergbetentisse. Germ. vergessenheit.
Ana, Extra vel Præter] Huic affine Sax. & nostrum Un, uti & Teutonicor. Dn, de quo vide Kilian. Etymolog. in Dn.
Arug, Perversa: nos Arg] Hac de voce vide doctiss. Spelmanni Glossar. in Arga.
main_text.head: Verba.

page.notes: Old English characters (/Æ, ᵹ, ɥ) and the black letter headwords are transcribed as best read; forms such as "/Ætulman", "aɥran" and "ofenzÿtolnerre" are uncertain. The last line is cut off at the foot of the page.
